A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Superposition Yields Robust Neural Scaling. All 37 pages, including Figures 1–23 and Appendices A–D, are readable and support comparison through text extraction and rendered-page inspection.

before.justification: v3 reports original toy-model experiments and LLM loss, representation-overlap and token-frequency analyses in Section 3 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental and data-analysis results, including the toy-model scaling experiments and LLM measurements.

M1.justification: The autoencoder, sampling procedure, reconstruction loss and weight-decay/growth update in Equation (2) are unchanged. Correcting norm delimiters in the following sentence does not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same synthetic feature distributions and language-modeling coverage using Wikitext-103, Pile-10k, C4 and BookCorpus. Appendices B–D introduce no coverage changes.

E2.justification: The weak/strong-superposition comparisons and random-vector/ETF references are retained. The empirical LLM analysis still includes OPT, GPT-2, Qwen2.5 and Pythia, with no comparator additions or removals.

E3.justification: Appendices B–D retain identical model dimensions, training budgets, preprocessing, metrics and fitting procedures, including evaluation on 10,000 text segments with maximum length 2048 tokens.

E4.justification: The frequency and weight-decay scans, activation-density analyses in Figures 14–15, larger-width experiment in Figure 18 and supplementary LLM analyses are unchanged. The discussion revision adds no analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same single-evaluation and seed statements in Appendix C.2, batch-loss standard deviations in Appendix D.1, and standard-error reporting for scaling exponents.

E6.justification: All numerical and plotted results are unchanged, including the LLM scaling exponent 0.91 ± 0.04 in Figure 6 and the Chinchilla-derived exponent 0.88 ± 0.06 in Section 3.3. Appendix results also match.

T1.justification: The sentence following Equation (2) replaces single bars with double norm bars, standardizing notation. The update equation, mathematical assumptions and derivations, including Appendices A and D, remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The claims about weak-superposition scaling, robust inverse-width scaling under strong superposition and agreement with LLM measurements are retained. The abstract’s replacement of 'like one over' with 'inversely with' is synonymous.

C2.justification: Section 5 replaces sentence-length/vocabulary sparsity reasoning with sparsity of tokens needed for prediction and explicitly proposes softmax error correction as favoring superposition. It drops the separate cross-entropy suggestion and softens 'not studied' to 'not studied in detail', while retaining the lack-of-rigorous-solution caveat.

D1.justification: The hyperparameters, hardware, data-processing instructions, script names and code-access disclosure are unchanged. Appendices B and C contain no added or revised reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 4 and all 63 references are unchanged. The relationship to Anthropic’s toy model, previous scaling explanations and representation-superposition research remains the same.

P1.justification: v4 lightly edits the abstract, standardizes norm notation and rewrites the opening discussion paragraph. The arXiv version/date stamp changes, while section order and the remaining narrative, including appendices, are retained.

P2.justification: All 23 figures, captions, axes, legends and placements are unchanged. Rendered comparison confirms identical appendix pages and retained page layout; differences are confined to local text, notation and the version stamp.

improvement.justification: v4 makes the norm notation consistent with Equation (2) and makes the tentative softmax/error-correction rationale more explicit in Section 5, while preserving the unsolved-toy-model caveat. These offer small clarity gains; the empirical evidence, derivations and principal limitations remain unchanged.
